decisions.reason: As a young software-based extension of the firm's core authentication and secure communication offer in a growing market, it still has option value and likely low carrying cost.
Mobile PDF signing is close to the established identity and authorization portfolio, so management would usually keep it while market demand and integration potential continue to resolve.
A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture fits the firm's deep cryptography capabilities and broader platform direction, making it a strong option to retain.
This message-delivery robot is adjacent to the core offer but more niche and potentially overlapping with other secure-channel products, so it is riskier yet still worth keeping for now.

A QR-code-based hardware signature token likely has higher carrying and support costs and fits less well with the firm's move toward app-based cross-channel identity solutions, so the option is weaker.
A payment-network security compliance suite builds on the firm's regulatory-security strengths, and in a growing industry it remains a plausible option despite some specialization.
